- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a downward correction of 2–5% for the following 5-day horizon.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 3–7% for the next 5 days.
- Model tends to lag mean reversion by 2–4 days; if sentiment shifts from neutral to bullish, forecast should start rising 1–2 days earlier than true outcome.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; cap forecast at 10% above recent 7-day average for first 5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model exhibits high variance; use median of 7-day moving average as baseline for correction.
